gap: The Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release used by the paper has only train (120k) and test (7.6k); the paper says the learning rate is selected on a validation set from {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} but the validation split is not part of the release.
chosen: Carve a 10% holdout (12,000 lines) out of the 120k training set with a fixed shuffle seed, group byte-identical duplicate articles together so the two parts share no text, select lr by mean validation accuracy over 3 fastText seeds, then retrain on the full 120k and evaluate on the untouched 7,600-line test split.
rationale: Keeps the official test split untouched (no test-set tuning) and follows the paper's grid search protocol; duplicate grouping removes leakage from the 135 duplicate lines present in AG News.

gap: Engine: the host is Windows 11 with no make/g++/clang/cmake, so the authors' Makefile / `pip install .` native build path (setup.py hard-codes -O3 -funroll-loops -pthread -march=native) is unavailable.
chosen: Use fasttext-wheel 0.9.2, a prebuilt binary wheel of the same facebookresearch/fastText 0.9.2 C++ trainer + official Python binding; reproduce.py still tries an importable fasttext module, then the wheel, then the native build, and only then the EmbeddingBag re-implementation (which would downgrade the verdict).
rationale: Same upstream source and same src/args.cc options as the CLI used in the paper; no author code is modified and every hyperparameter is forwarded verbatim.

gap: Section 2.2 says to use 10M hashing bins "if only bigrams are used" and 100M otherwise; the paper's Table 1 rows use bigrams, but the author script uses a single -bucket 10000000 for all datasets.
chosen: bucket = 10,000,000, matching the authors' own classification-results.sh; the paper's alternative 100M-bin setting is not used because 100M bins x dim 10 x 4 B = ~4 GB for the input matrix alone on a 15.4 GB machine that also holds the C++ training copies and the test set. The deviation is logged in results/metrics.json.
rationale: The authors' released Table 1 reproduction script uses 10M bins, so this matches the code that produced the published numbers; memory is also a constraint.

gap: The paper reports one number per configuration and fastText's asynchronous multi-threaded SGD with 20 threads is not run-to-run deterministic (~0.1-0.3% spread); a single run would not distinguish method noise from a reproduction gap.
chosen: Report C1/C2 as the mean over 5 fastText RNG seeds (per-seed values and std in results/metrics.json) and average each lr-grid point over 3 seeds when selecting lr.
rationale: Quantifies run-to-run noise so the verifier can judge the gap from the paper's value; also makes the lr selection stable instead of a coin flip between 0.1 and 0.25.
